title: SA/137/2018 of HARI SINGH Vs GURMEET SINGH

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Second Appeal No. 137 of 2018
Hari Singh and others .....Appellants
Versus
Gurmeet Singh ...Respondent
Advocate: Mr. Abhishek Verma, Advocate for the appellants
Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
The grievance of the present defendant/appellant in the
Second Appeal is against the judgement dated 17.09.2018 as rendered
by the Court of 1st Additional District Judge, Kashipur, District
Udham Singh Nagar in Civil Appeal No. 63 of 2014 (Computer Filing
Civil Appeal No. 02 of 2015), Hari Singh and others Vs. Gurmeet
Singh, whereby the appeal of defendant-appellant was dismissed by
impugned judgement dated 17.09.2018, consequently the appellate
court has affirmed the judgement dated 26.08.2014 as rendered in Suit
filed by the plaintiff-respondent being Suit No. 26 of 2010, Gurmeet
Singh Vs. Hari Singh and others, whereby in the Suit in question of
respondent, the plaintiff (respondent herein) had prayed for decree of
permanent injunction in relation to the property which has been more
particularly described at the foot of the plaint, constituted to be a land
lying in khata No. 00033, khasra No. 541 having an area of 0.6590
hectares and khasra No. 547A having an area of 0.2490 hectares i.e. in
total area of 0.9080 hectares.

2. The admitted fact, which has emerged as per the plaint
allegation instituted on 28.11.2010 and even as per the averments

2
made in the written statement filed on March 2010 by the present
appellants before this Court is that the aforesaid disputed land which
was lying in khata 00033 of village Bhawanipur, Tehsil Jaspur,
admittedly the plaintiff-respondent are the recorded bhumidhars of the
property in question which has been more particularly detailed in the
plaint map shown by figure A, B,C, D, only issue was that defendant-appellant claim his plot allegedly khasra J48 and 536 is adjoining to
disputed land.
3. It was also specifically pleaded by the plaintiff-respondent that he is the owner of the property having purchased the
same by virtue of a sale deed which was executed in his favour and he
had specifically demarcated the property by laying down merth
/boundaries of the respective passage of the land.
4. The plaintiffs in the Suit had contended that the
respondent by way of an arbitrary action dated 20.01.2010 wanted to
encroach upon the land belonging to the plaintiffs which gave a cause
of action of suit and hence the respondent instituted a suit for a decree
of permanent injunction on 28.01.2010. In the said Suit, the appellants
had put in appearance and had filed their written statement on March
2010.
5. What is important to be remarked from the pleadings
raised in the written statement by the respondent is that the
defendants-appellants herein admit the fact that the plaintiff is the
recorded bhumidhar of the land lying in khasra Nos. 541 and 547M
(disputed land). They further admit the fact that the plaintiff is in
possession of aforesaid land in dispute in his exclusive right. In
defence, the defendant/appellants have submitted and claimed that
they are the owners of khasra No. 548 and 536 which, according to
them their land is adjoining to the land of the plaintiff/respondent
which is subject matter of the dispute in the suit and their case was
that taking advantage of the land lying adjacent to the disputed
property, the plaintiff is trying to encroach upon the said land.

3
6. The defendants-appellants further submitted that in order
to remove the anomaly in the identifiability of the land, which
admittedly according to the defendants-appellants happens to be
adjoining to one another, the defendants-appellants have already
initiated the proceedings under Section 41 of the Land Revenue Act,
which has been registered as Case No. 5/7 of 2008-09 in which the
measurement was done by the competent authority under the Land
Revenue Act, 1901 on 02.02.2009 and the report was produced before
the Sub-Divisional Magistrate.
7. However, as there being some anomaly in the report
dated 02.02.2009 thus submitted. The re-measurement/re-survey was
done in the said proceedings in continuance to the proceedings under
Section 41 of the Land Revenue Act and the same is pending
consideration for recovery before the Sub-Judicial Magistrate.
8. The argument of the learned counsel for the appellants is
that since the proceedings under Section 41 of the Land Revenue Act
which is a demarcation proceeding for identifiability of land and same
is pending before the Sub-Divisional Magistrate. The Civil Court,
while entertaining and considering the suit for permanent injunction
ought to have desisted from passing the decree of permanent
injunction in favour of the plaintiff on 26.09.2014 in the absence of
there being an identifibility of land on the culmination of proceedings
under Section 41 of the Land Revenue Act.
9. This argument as extended by the learned counsel for the
appellants is not acceptable by this Court for the following reasons:-
(i) That the proceedings under Section 41 of the Land
Revenue Act are summary proceedings and summary
proceedings will never create any embargo in initiation
or pendency of proceeding under Section 9 of the Code
of Civil Procedure, which is a regular proceeding for
grant of a decree prayed for by the plaintiff.

4
(ii) Even otherwise also, the proceedings under Section 41 of
the Land Revenue Act since being always a subject
matter of a judicious scrutiny in the proceedings of
appeal under Section 210, and thereafter under statutory
revision under Section 219 of the Land Revenue Act yet
again it will not pose any restriction in proceedings with
the suit for grant of decree of permanent injunction.
(iii) Even otherwise also the proceedings under Land
Revenue Act has not been given an overriding effect.
10. Besides this, when the Court proceeded with the matter
and the parties were directed to lead their respective evidence, it has
come on record that in between the property in dispute of plaintiff and
the property of the defendants lying in khasra No. 548 and 536, there
lies another intervening property, which separates them and the land
of plaintiff in dispute is not adjoining to the land of the defendants.
11. It has been a specific case taken up by the plaintiff in one
of the documents submitted by him before the learned trial Court as
Paper No. 31 Ka that as far as the plaintiff's khasra Nos. 541 and 547
are concerned, for which decree of permanent injunction was sought
for, in fact, is surrounded by the revenue boundary wall/mer, and at no
point the said boundary /mer has been shown as common to the mer
of the land of the defendant.
12. On exchange of the pleadings, learned trial Court had
framed the following issues:

13. Since as per the pleadings raised in the written statement,
and as per the documents placed on record, there was no controversy
that the plaintiff-respondent is a recorded owner of the property in
dispute in the suit No. 26/2010, and he owns a title over the property
hence the issue no. 1 pertaining to the ownership, possession and title
was decided in favour of the plaintiff-respondent while rendering
judgement on issue No. 1.
14. As far as issue No. 2 is concerned, the pleadings
pertaining to an act of encroachment made by the appellants on
20.01.2010 which was cause of action for suit, the Court after
considering the statement of PW-2 Balbir Singh and the affidavit filed
in support thereof Paper No. 56 Ka/2 and the statement of PW-3
Yashvir Singh has come to the conclusion that in the affidavit in
examination-in-chief filed by the defendants-appellants as PW-1, the
defendants had not specifically denied of having made an effort to
encroach upon the land of the plaintiff as pleaded to be the cause of
action in the suit. Both the courts have concurrently recorded the
findings against the defendant-appellant.
15. Similarly, issue no. 3 pertaining to the maintainability of
the proceedings in view of the bar created under Section 331 of the
U.P.Z.A. and L.R. Act. Admittedly, when the defendants plead the
ownership of the plaintiff and having not denied the same and when
he pleads the possession to be with the defendants, the bar of Section
331 would have only come into play when there involves any intricate
issue on determination of title of the rival parties to the proceedings or
has an element of declaration of title which is not the case at hand.
Hence a simplicitor suit for grant of an injunction for restraining from
an act of interference without there being any element of seeking a
declaration as against the property in dispute it would not bar the suit
for an injunction under Section 331 of the U.P.Z.A. & L.R. Act.
16. On concluding of the aforesaid proceedings, the learned
trial Court by its judgment dated 26.08.2014 had decreed the suit of

6
the plaintiff-respondent against which the defendants-appellants
herein preferred a First Appeal being Appeal No. 63 of 2014, Hari
Singh and others Vs. Gurmeet Singh under Section 96 of Code of
Civil Procedure. The said appeal too, on considering the rival
contentions, the Appellate Court had dismissed the appeal by
impugned judgment dated 17.09.2018 which is also under challenge
before this Court.
17. In view of what has been observed above, this Court is of
the opinion that so far as the question of an act of interference as made
by defendant on 20.02.2010, has been concurrently recorded against
the defendants, more particularly, in the light of the fact that when the
said pleading was not controverted by the defendants in the pleading
as made in the written statement. Furthermore, the finding pertaining
to the exclusive ownership of the disputed property, being vested with
the plaintiff too since stand admitted in view of the pleading raised in
the written statement, thus when the finding of title, ownership and act
of interference would be concurrent in nature. Hence, this Second
Appeal does not involve any substantial question of law which
requires to be answered by this Court, consequently, the Second
Appeal fails and is accordingly dismissed.
18. However, having said so and while dismissing the
present Second Appeal, it will not create any embargo so far it relates
to the adjudication of the proceedings under Section 41 of the Land
Revenue Act is concerned which has been initiated by the defendants-appellants. Consequently, the present Second Appeal fails and is
hereby dismissed. No order as to costs.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 18.12.2018
